scope.repairFocus: Circadian relationship, grammar/completion defects, ML evaluation provenance, athlete-data governance, ethics/consent, supplement risk, and return-to-sport provenance.

changes.revisedText: Centre of pressure is defined as:
changes.reviewerNote: Removed the duplicate article while preserving the force-plate concept and answer key.

changes.revisedText: A regression slope of 0.4 means a one-unit predictor increase is associated with:
changes.reviewerNote: Revised the stem so the option is a grammatical completion.

changes.revisedText: A frequentist 95% CI procedure means about 95% of repeated intervals contain:
changes.reviewerNote: Removed the duplicated article before the keyed population-parameter option.

revisedOptions: wider overall
narrower overall
exactly zero
unrelated to standard error
changes.reviewerNote: Converted the options into grammatical complements of 'makes a CI'.

changes.revisedText: In a symmetric CI, the point estimate is at:
revisedOptions: lower confidence limit
upper confidence limit
confidence-level value
centre of the interval
changes.reviewerNote: Removed repeated articles so all options complete the revised stem consistently.

changes.revisedText: Cohen's d is a mean difference divided by:
revisedOptions: the number of participants in each sample
the reported p-value from the comparison
the selected confidence level
the pooled standard deviation
changes.reviewerNote: Removed the duplicated article while preserving the effect-size definition and key.

changes.revisedExplanation: Data leakage occurs when information unavailable at prediction time, such as a post-injury variable, is used to build the model and produces over-optimistic performance estimates.
changes.reviewerNote: Assigned a directly relevant official source for the data-leakage definition and aligned the explanation to it.

changes.revisedExplanation: Sensitivity, also called recall for the positive class, is the proportion of actual positive cases that the classifier correctly identifies.
changes.reviewerNote: Assigned an official classification-metrics source and made the explanation directly support sensitivity/recall.

changes.revisedExplanation: With rare injury cases, a model can obtain high accuracy by predicting the common non-injury class while missing the minority injury cases, so prevalence and class-specific metrics matter.
changes.reviewerNote: Assigned an official model-evaluation source and explicitly justified the class-imbalance concern.
Remapped the athlete-management-system definition to the directly relevant official athlete-data-governance source.

revisedOptions: The body clock has already delayed beyond the destination time

changes.revisedExplanation: After westward travel, the athlete may need a phase delay; early local-evening sleepiness can reflect an internal clock that remains relatively late or advanced for the destination time.
changes.reviewerNote: Corrected the westward-travel phase relationship while preserving the keyed index and travel-readiness concept.
